question: Why can changing feature scale change a model’s behavior even when the underlying data pattern is the same?
direct_answer: Because many algorithms are not scale-invariant, so rescaling changes distances, gradients, and tradeoffs between features.
expanded_answer: A feature’s numeric scale affects how an algorithm interprets it. In distance-based methods, larger-scale features contribute more to distances. In gradient-based optimization, poorly scaled features can create ill-conditioned loss landscapes, making training slow or unstable. In regularized models, scale can also affect how strongly each coefficient is penalized. So the same conceptual dataset can lead to very different fitted models if its features are rescaled differently.
key_points: Scale affects distances in geometric methods
Scale affects optimization conditioning in gradient methods
Scale can change the effect of regularization
common_wrong_ideas: Models only care about the underlying ranking, never numeric scale
Rescaling features cannot change the learned parameters
Scaling matters only for neural networks
